nodes.title: Sol 1: Dust Storm Alarm
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Satellites in space spotted a small storm before it grew huge.
nodes.storyText: Look out! Orbiting satellites just spotted a tiny dust storm heading your way. The sky is bright this Martian Sol as dust lifts water vapor.
nodes.guideTip: Whoa! A Sol is one day on Mars. It is slightly longer than Earth days!
nodes.novaHint: The storm is coming. Think about saving power before dust blocks sunlight.

choiceA.description: Bring astronauts inside and pack solar power into batteries.
choiceA.outcomeText: Batteries fill with power! The crew is safe inside, but stops outdoor work.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Opportunity ran on solar power for 14 years. A giant storm blocked the sun.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Without power, robots and heaters freeze in the deep Martian cold.
choiceA.guideReaction: Full batteries! Smart move before the sky goes dark.

choiceB.description: Let the crew collect ice and fill oxygen tanks.
choiceB.outcomeText: Oxygen tanks are full! The drill motors use lots of battery power.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Curiosity used a tiny nuclear battery. It kept rolling right through the storm.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Nuclear power does not need sunlight to make electricity.
choiceB.guideReaction: Lots of oxygen! Pumps use power, but fresh air is great.

choiceC.description: Bring the crew inside and turn on electric dust shields.
choiceC.outcomeText: Electric shields push dust away from solar panels and airlocks!
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: NASA created shields that use static electricity to push away dust.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Mars dust carries static cling, just like dust on a TV screen.
choiceC.guideReaction: Zap! The electric shields shake the red dust away!

nodes.title: Sol 2: Dust Hits Panels
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: In 2018, rising dust forced Opportunity to stop driving.
nodes.storyText: A giant dust wall towers more than 37 miles high! Sticky red grit clings to panels. You must also keep rocket fuel cold.
nodes.guideTip: The storm is huge! It is taller than seven Mount Everests stacked up!
nodes.novaHint: Cold fuel is heavy. Balance rocket coolers with life support power.

consequences.text: Sol 1 extra battery charge helped (+3% Electricity), but missing ice frustrated crew (-3% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Chill rocket fuel and dim hallway lights to save power.
choiceA.outcomeText: Rocket fuel stays freezing cold! Hallways are dim, but batteries stay safe.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Rocket fuel must stay colder than winter ice so it does not boil.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Liquid fuel boils away into gas if tanks get too warm.
choiceA.guideReaction: Brrr! Hallways are chilly, but the escape rocket is safe!

choiceB.description: Use battery power to make fresh, clean oxygen.
choiceB.outcomeText: Crisp oxygen fills every room! The crew feels great, but batteries drain.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: NASA tested MOXIE on Mars. It pulls breathable oxygen right from thin air.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Mars air is mostly carbon dioxide, which humans cannot breathe.
choiceB.guideReaction: Deep breath! Clean oxygen makes everyone smile and work happily.

choiceC.description: Power up the dish to track the storm from orbit.
choiceC.outcomeText: Clear radar maps show the storm! Running the dish heater uses power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Orbiting satellites tracked the 2018 dust storm every single day.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Satellites fly high above storms to guide rovers safely.
choiceC.guideReaction: We see the whole storm! Look at that giant swirling cloud!

nodes.title: Sol 2: Yellow Grid Warning
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Mars dust clings to solar panels like static on clothes.
nodes.storyText: Dust covers your panels, just like on Opportunity rover! Oxygen is high, but greenhouse crops need light. Red sticky grit is everywhere.
nodes.guideTip: Plants in the greenhouse need bright lamps because Mars is dim!
nodes.novaHint: Plants make food, but need power. Decide how much energy to spend.

consequences.text: Full oxygen tanks from Sol 1 kept crew energized (+5% Crew Health), using power (-4% Power).

choiceA.description: Turn off plant grow-lights to save electricity for basic needs.
choiceA.outcomeText: Saving power keeps the base alive! The plants grow slower in the dark.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts will grow fresh greens in space to stay strong and healthy.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Plants turn light and water into fresh food and clean oxygen.
choiceA.guideReaction: Lights off saves power! The lettuce will take a little nap.

choiceB.description: Spend battery power on bright grow-lights for fresh veggies.
choiceB.outcomeText: Fresh salad lifts everyone's spirits! Battery power drops down lower.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts on the space station grow fresh salads under bright LED lights.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Fresh vitamins keep human minds sharp during long space voyages.
choiceB.guideReaction: Mmm, fresh green snacks! The crew is super happy today.

choiceC.description: Turn up the backup nuclear reactor to make steady electricity.
choiceC.outcomeText: The reactor hums with power! It generates electricity without any sun.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: NASA tested small nuclear reactors to power future human Mars bases.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Nuclear reactors make electricity through day, night, and giant storms.
choiceC.guideReaction: Power surge! The tiny nuclear core makes steady watts in the dark.

nodes.title: Sol 2: Dust on Airlocks
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Static electric charge makes Mars dust cling to everything.
nodes.storyText: Electric shields fight off sticky red grit. We cannot wait for dust devils! Fine powder drifts toward airlock suit doors.
nodes.guideTip: Mars dust is like tiny bits of broken glass. Keep it outside!
nodes.novaHint: Clean airlocks protect human lungs. Balance door shields with power.

consequences.text: Clean Sol 1 dust shields saved gear (+4% Crew Health), using power (-4% Power).

choiceA.description: Power door cleaners so zero dust enters astronaut lungs.
choiceA.outcomeText: Airlocks stay clean and dust-free! The door shields use steady power.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: NASA designs suits that stay outside the cabin to block poisonous dust.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Breathing sharp mineral dust can hurt astronaut lungs.
choiceA.guideReaction: Puff! High-voltage zap cleans suits before astronauts step inside.

choiceB.description: Connect nuclear power straight to batteries and dim heaters.
choiceB.outcomeText: Batteries charge steadily! Corridors are chilly, but power is strong.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Engineers route nuclear electricity to protect life-support batteries first.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Nuclear power provides constant electricity without cloudy day drops.
choiceB.guideReaction: Nice connection! Power flows right where we need it most.

choiceC.description: Send crew outside to add weatherproof shields to electronics.
choiceC.outcomeText: Electronics are safe from grit! The outdoor walk tired the crew.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Spacewalks on Mars take careful effort because spacesuits are stiff.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Spacesuit gloves make simple tool work feel like squeezing tennis balls.
choiceC.guideReaction: Good job fixing the box! Those spacesuits are heavy work.

nodes.title: Sol 3: Red Dusk Falling
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Dust traps daytime heat, making cold Mars nights warmer.
nodes.storyText: Dust dims the Sun in thin Martian air! Dust starts a heat blanket at dusk as oxygen generators pull power.
nodes.guideTip: Even in thin air, dust traps warm heat near the ground at night!
nodes.novaHint: When solar fades, manage your life support and heater watts carefully.

consequences.text: Locked chillers saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but chilly halls gave stiff joints (-4% Crew Health).
Sleeping crops saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but missing fresh veggies lowers stamina (-5% Crew Health).
Sol 1 extra battery charge still cushions the power grid (+3% Electricity).
Reserve oxygen from Sol 1 keeps air fresh (+4% Crew Health), using valve power (-3% Power).

choiceA.description: Close empty side labs and gather the crew in central bunks.
choiceA.outcomeText: Sealing side labs saves big power! Outer halls get icy cold.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts close doors between modules to trap warm air and save power.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Closing hatches prevents cold drafts from spreading across the station.
choiceA.guideReaction: Hatches sealed tight! Heat stays inside the center habitat.

choiceB.description: Spend battery power to scrub carbon dioxide and pump oxygen.
choiceB.outcomeText: Crisp oxygen fills living rooms! The heavy air pumps use power.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Life support systems must scrub carbon dioxide so humans can breathe clean air.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Without scrubbers, carbon dioxide builds up and makes astronauts sleepy.
choiceB.guideReaction: Ahhh, fresh air! Crisp oxygen helps everyone think clearly.

choiceC.description: Download satellite storm maps so astronauts stay safe indoors.
choiceC.outcomeText: Satellites show storm tracks! Downloading radar maps uses modest power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Satellites in high orbit track dust fronts and beam weather maps down.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Orbiters can see storm fronts hundreds of miles away.
choiceC.guideReaction: Radar locked! Now we know exactly when gusts hit.

nodes.title: Sol 3: Sky Dimming Fast
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Mars dust storms can swallow the entire planet in days.
nodes.storyText: Dusk falls at noon as a planet-wide storm grows! The sky nears noon pitch black. Greenhouse crops compete with sensors for power.
nodes.guideTip: The storm wraps around the whole planet! There is no escape route.
nodes.novaHint: A whole-planet storm lasts weeks. Pace food, water, and power.

consequences.text: Boosted MOXIE oxygen keeps crew sharp (+5% Crew Health), using power (-4% Power).
Fresh salad greens boost crew stamina (+5% Crew Health), using power (-4% Power).
Electric airlock shields keep dust out of lungs (+4% Crew Health), using power (-3% Power).
Sol 1 dust shields shook static grit off panels (0% Electricity Conserved!).

choiceA.description: Dim cabin lights and heaters to save power before blackout.
choiceA.outcomeText: Saving power protects the batteries! Rooms are chilly and dim.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Spacecraft turn off non-essential instruments during power emergencies.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Cutting cabin lights saves precious battery watts for life support.
choiceA.guideReaction: Heaters dimmed! Every saved watt keeps life support alive.

choiceB.description: Keep bright lights glowing so fresh crops keep growing.
choiceB.outcomeText: Fresh green sprouts lift spirits! The grow-lights draw heavy power.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts grow fresh salad crops under LED lamps for vitamins.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Plants provide psychological comfort along with fresh oxygen and nutrition.
choiceB.guideReaction: Yum, crunchy fresh leaves! The crew is smiling big.

choiceC.description: Cut crew heaters to power wind radar and study the storm.
choiceC.outcomeText: Sensors track the storm front! Chilly drafts sweep the dorms.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Scientists track atmospheric pressure to understand how dust storms grow.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Understanding storm physics helps NASA design safer future habitats.
choiceC.guideReaction: Science data incoming! Fascinating storm measurements today.

nodes.title: Sol 3: Nuclear Core Hums
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Nuclear generators keep running right through deep darkness.
nodes.storyText: Red dusk falls, but just like Curiosity kept working, your nuclear power plant hums! You must also keep rocket fuel cold.
nodes.guideTip: The nuclear reactor makes electricity inside, even when the sun vanishes!
nodes.novaHint: Nuclear power is steady. Decide whether to cool equipment or crew.

consequences.text: Nuclear power gave steady electricity (+3% Electricity), but loud shielding bunks tired crew (-4% Crew Health).
Direct reactor connection filled batteries (+3% Electricity), but cold galley lowered comfort (-4% Crew Health).
Oxygen stockpile keeps air easy to breathe (+4% Crew Health), using minor power (-3% Power).
Sol 1 dust shields shook static grit off panels (0% Electricity Conserved!).

choiceA.description: Move astronauts into narrow ground tunnels to save fan power.
choiceA.outcomeText: Tunnels save heating power! Tight bunks make sleep uncomfortable.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Mars dirt protects astronauts from space radiation and temperature swings.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Burying habitats under regolith dirt provides natural thermal insulation.
choiceA.guideReaction: Cozy underground! Natural dirt keeps the cold wind away.

choiceB.description: Run cooling fans at full speed so crew stays comfortable.
choiceB.outcomeText: The reactor core stays cool and happy! Batteries drop down.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Nuclear systems need radiator fans to dump extra heat safely.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Radiators pump fluid through fins to radiate heat into space.
choiceB.guideReaction: Cool and steady! The reactor hums smoothly tonight.

choiceC.description: Send crew outside to bolt protective dust covers onto turbines.
choiceC.outcomeText: Turbines are shielded from grit! The dusty outdoor walk tired crew.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Covering mechanical joints keeps fine grit from grinding gears down.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Sharp Martian dust acts like sandpaper on moving turbine parts.
choiceC.guideReaction: Turbine covers bolted! The cooling fins are safe from grit.

nodes.title: Sol 3: Radio Static Haze
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Satellites fly high above storms to relay radio signals.
nodes.storyText: Dust haze creates a murky sky view! An orbital satellite talks across a 22-minute radio delay as electric shields hum.
nodes.guideTip: Satellites in space act like cell towers to send radio messages home!
nodes.novaHint: Earth messages take 22 minutes. Rely on local plans and rovers.

consequences.text: Satellite weather maps boosted crew readiness (+4% Crew Health), using power (-3% Power).
Cleaned panels kept power flow steady (0% Electricity Conserved!), but dust irritated throats (-4% Crew Health).
Sol 1 battery vault still cushions the darkening sky (+3% Electricity).
Sol 1 dust shields continue repelling fine grit outdoors (0% Electricity Conserved!).

choiceA.description: Turn off radio dish heaters to save battery power before blackout.
choiceA.outcomeText: Saving power protects the batteries! We lose live messages from Earth.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Turning off powerful transmitters saves big wattage during storms.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: High-gain antennas use lots of electricity to beam signals to Earth.
choiceA.guideReaction: Antennas sleeping! That saves lots of power for life support.

choiceB.description: Send crew outside to crimp tight dust sleeves over junction boxes.
choiceB.outcomeText: Junction boxes are sealed from grit! Cold windy work tired the crew.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts wrap wiring boxes with silicone sleeves to stop shorts.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Dry static dust can cause electrical sparks if it gets inside plugs.
choiceB.guideReaction: Cables sealed tight! No short circuits will happen here.

choiceC.description: Plug pressurized rover fuel cells into the habitat filter bus.
choiceC.outcomeText: Rover fuel cells share extra power! Cabin air stays warm and clean.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Electric vehicles can feed battery power back into buildings in emergencies.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Connecting rover batteries gives the habitat extra backup power.
choiceC.guideReaction: Rover connected! Extra power is flowing right into the habitat.

nodes.title: Sol 4: Midnight at Noon
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: By Sol 4, the 2018 storm blocked 99% of daylight.
nodes.storyText: Dust blocks 97% of normal sunlight, just like on Opportunity rover! Batteries must fight to keep rocket fuel cold.
nodes.guideTip: It is totally black at lunchtime! Solar panels make zero electricity.
nodes.novaHint: Solar is out. Protect the cold rocket fuel for your flight home.

consequences.text: Sealed corridors save power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but chilly rooms stiffen joints (-4% Crew Health).
Pre-locked chillers saved battery voltage (0% Electricity Conserved!), but rationing lowered comfort (-3% Crew Health).
Sol 1 dust shields stopped electrical short circuits (0% Electricity Conserved!).
Rationed heat saved battery charge (0% Electricity Conserved!), but cold leaves crew stiff (-3% Crew Health).
Powering down the dish conserved electricity (0% Electricity Conserved!), but silence causes loneliness (-3% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Pump power into rocket chillers while crew bundles in coats.
choiceA.outcomeText: Rocket fuel stays safe and frozen! The habitat feels chilly.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Rocket propellants like liquid methane must stay chilled at -297°F.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: If tanks warm up, liquid fuel boils into gas and escapes into space.
choiceA.guideReaction: Rocket fuel safe! Our ride back to Earth is protected.

choiceB.description: Dial back outdoor fuel chillers so the crew stays warm indoors.
choiceB.outcomeText: Warm air fills the dome! Rocket tank gauges show slight warming.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Keeping astronauts warm prevents hypothermia and maintains mental focus.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Cold stress lowers human immune defenses and slows reaction times.
choiceB.guideReaction: Nice and warm! Happy astronauts can solve any problem.

choiceC.description: Shut down science rooms and hallway heat to guard battery power.
choiceC.outcomeText: Battery drain stops! Astronauts rest quietly in dim, chilly bunks.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Deep space probes enter beacon mode to survive power emergencies.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Beacon mode runs only vital computer clocks and emergency radios.
choiceC.guideReaction: Beacon mode locked! Every single watt is guarded.

nodes.title: Sol 4: Storm Peaks Outside
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Dust trapped near the ground acts like an insulating thermal blanket.
nodes.storyText: Dust blocks 97% of normal sunlight! Thick dust acts like a blanket trapping heat near ground against airlock suitports.
nodes.guideTip: The storm is at peak strength! The dust blanket keeps nights warmer.
nodes.novaHint: This is the darkest day. Keep crew morale strong and grit outside.

consequences.text: Greenhouse plant lights draw steady power (-4% Power), but fresh greens boost stamina (+5% Crew Health).
Clean MOXIE air purge from Sol 3 kept cabin air crisp and sharp (+5% Crew Health).
Upgraded suit seals stop fine red powder at the airlock (+4% Crew Health).
Tunnel bunks saved power (0% Electricity Conserved!), but tight quarters left muscles cramped (-3% Crew Health).

choiceA.description: Turn down electric heaters and have everyone wear thick parkas.
choiceA.outcomeText: Thick parkas save power! Working in bulky coats tires the crew.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Thermal survival gear keeps astronauts warm when electrical heat is cut.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Multi-layer insulation traps body heat with reflective silver film.
choiceA.guideReaction: Parkas zipped up! Warm coats save lots of battery power.

choiceB.description: Run kitchen stoves and bright lamps for a happy hot dinner.
choiceB.outcomeText: Hot stew lifts everyone's spirits! Kitchen stoves use battery power.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Sharing a hot meal boosts team morale during dark space emergencies.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Warm comfort food keeps astronaut spirits high during long crises.
choiceB.guideReaction: Dinner is served! Hot food makes this dark day bright.

choiceC.description: Pressurize airlock doors so swirling grit cannot enter rooms.
choiceC.outcomeText: Door curtains keep dust out! Running the pumps uses battery power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Positive air pressure pushes dust outward when airlock doors open.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Air pressure differences keep fine minerals from floating into cabins.
choiceC.guideReaction: Air curtains on! Not a single speck of dust gets inside.

nodes.title: Sol 4: Clogged Air Filters
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Curiosity rolled on nuclear power while dust coated Gale Crater.
nodes.storyText: Curiosity rolled safely on nuclear power, but humans breathe air! Sticky red grit just clogged filters. The MOXIE oxygen maker needs airflow.
nodes.guideTip: Human astronauts breathe air. Robots only need electrical power!
nodes.novaHint: Clogged filters strain lungs. Clean them now or switch to spares.

consequences.text: Sol 3 storm sensors still drain circuits (-5% Power), though alerts helped (+2% Crew Health).
Steady reactor cooling kept electronics safe (+3% Crew Health).
Reactor bypass overheated coils (-5% Power) and was noisy (-3% Crew Health).
Sealed power ducts protected cables from dust (0% Electricity Conserved!).

choiceA.description: Wear masks and clean dust out of main cabin air filters.
choiceA.outcomeText: Clean air flows through the dome! Cleaning filters was tiring work.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Space crews clean life support filters regularly to maintain clean air.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: HEPA air filters catch microscopic dust particles before lungs inhale them.
choiceA.guideReaction: Scrub scrub scrub! Clean airflow is back in every room.

choiceB.description: Keep fans running to save power without stopping to clean.
choiceB.outcomeText: Saving power protects batteries! Hazy cabin air makes crew cough.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Dust in cabin air causes eye irritation and respiratory coughing.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Mars mineral dust contains toxic perchlorates that irritate human lungs.
choiceB.guideReaction: Cough cough! Dusty air saves power, but tickles throats.

choiceC.description: Turn on smaller backup scrubbers and vent dust outside.
choiceC.outcomeText: Backup scrubbers clear the haze! The extra motors draw power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Manned space habitats carry dual backup systems for all vital equipment.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Redundant backup scrubbers kick in when primary units get clogged.
choiceC.guideReaction: Backup scrubbers online! Fresh air without the tiring scrubbing.

nodes.title: Sol 4: Signals in Blackout
nodes.nasaFactBanner: 2018 LESSON: Orbiting satellites stayed high above the dust to relay commands.
nodes.storyText: Dust clouds tower more than 37 miles high! An MRO relay satellite flies overhead. Balance parked rovers with your nuclear power plant.
nodes.guideTip: Satellites fly high in space where there is no dust storm at all!
nodes.novaHint: Satellites have storm maps from above. Think about connecting.

consequences.text: Aligning dishes on Sol 3 saved radio power (0% Electricity Conserved!).
Rover heaters ate power (-4% Power), but rovers stayed safe (+4% Crew Health).
Sol 2 satellite link gave clear updates (+2% Crew Health).
Reactor turbine shields protected power flow (0% Electricity Conserved!).

choiceA.description: Put outside rovers and antennas to sleep to save power.
choiceA.outcomeText: All watts stay inside the habitat! We lose satellite weather maps.
choiceA.nasaRealDecision: Probes sleep during deep cold to save battery life for emergencies.
choiceA.nasaFactEmphasis: Hibernating gear draws only tiny trickles of standby electricity.
choiceA.guideReaction: Rovers sleeping! Every watt is saved for life support.

choiceB.description: Send crew out to hook rover batteries into the habitat grid.
choiceB.outcomeText: Rover batteries boost base power! Hauling heavy cables tired the crew.
choiceB.nasaRealDecision: Electric vehicles can send battery power back into buildings in emergencies.
choiceB.nasaFactEmphasis: Connecting rover batteries gives the habitat a giant power bank.
choiceB.guideReaction: Plugged in! The rovers are powering the lights right now.

choiceC.description: Power the dish to get new storm maps and notes from Earth.
choiceC.outcomeText: Family letters bring big smiles! The big radio dish uses power.
choiceC.nasaRealDecision: Astronauts receive daily voice notes and emails from family on Earth.
choiceC.nasaFactEmphasis: Hearing loved ones is the number one morale booster in space.
choiceC.guideReaction: Letters from Earth! Everyone is smiling and reading warm notes.
